the common belief of rationality is not a property of most extensive form games, and that the common belief in rationality is a property of the extensive form games that are rationalizable by the Bernheim-Pearce theory.

The main takeaway from our work is that
in games with perfect information, the assumption of common belief of rationality is too strong to be a plausible assumption for the purpose of deriving a solution concept.
